speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the Ministry's operational definition of a "good job" as used in the Economic Strategy Review; (b) what measurable indicators will the Ministry use to track whether the strategy is creating such jobs; and (c) whether the Ministry will adopt a multi-dimensional job quality framework comparable to that published by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This enables comparisons across sectors, firms, occupations and workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Having said that, the notion of a "good job" varies across individuals, shaped by their circumstances and aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It often includes factors such as wage growth, opportunities for career development, fair and safe workplaces, personal fulfilment, and what gives someone highest utility, among many others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There are multiple dimensions to good jobs, and no single, universally accepted framework for measuring job quality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Local workers have experienced sustained and inclusive wage growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Two-thirds of private sector establishments provided structured training to employees, demonstrating that employers continue to invest in their workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We have also enacted the Workplace Fairness Act to promote fair employment practices and protect employees from workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We will continue working to ensure that our economic strategies translate economic growth into good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The Economic Strategy Review (ESR) mid-term update factsheet uses the phrase "good jobs" six times without defining it.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: My first supplementary question is, what is the issue with creating a job quality framework like the OECD has done?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Second is, I thank the Senior Minister of State for mentioning the different factors that he tracks.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, will the Government track this, to define this as part of their definition of a "good job"?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: My last supplementary question, the ESR also says it will uplift and transform roles like electricians and care workers.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But a commitment that cannot be proven true or false, is not really an accountable commitment.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, would the Ministry set clear benchmarks in terms of pay, progression and working conditions, so that Parliament can actually determine if uplift has occurred?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I guess, fundamentally, the workers are interested in whether their pay goes up.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For them, as I have said, a good job need not just be pay, but many other dimensions around it.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But fundamentally, workers want to see their wages go up from year to year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And in fact, as they get more seniority, they want to be recognised for their talent as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we do take reference from the wage distribution of our workforce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And by creating more of such jobs and helping more Singaporeans to upskill to take them on, we will grow the median wage of our workforce over time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is a useful indication of broad-based wage growth that also shows that with the measures that are put in, the median wage of individual workers goes up over time and as a workforce, it also rises.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Member's second question of looking at wage share, well, I think there are, like I said, there are multiple dimensions to track and we will continue to measure multiple dimensions of job quality, that could include looking at wage share over time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In doing so, we will consider relevant dimensions that are included in other international frameworks of job quality, including the one that the Member has mentioned – the OECD's job quality framework.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Member's third question on what the ESR is doing with regard to trade and skilled roles, this is an area still under deliberation by the ESR, so I would not jump the gun and make any pronouncements here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In time to come, when the ESR releases its final report, there will be a better treatment of the questions that the Member asked regarding trades and skilled roles.
